# Ratchet & Clank: Up Your Arsenal (2004)

The third Ratchet & Clank, released on the PlayStation 2 in 2004 (in Europe as *Ratchet & Clank 3*).
Both releases are decompiled in one repository, our rac3-decomp: PAL (`SCES-524.56`) is its
primary target, and NTSC-U (`SCUS-973.53`) is built from the same C
([decomp/docs/versions.md](decomp/docs/versions.md)).

## In this folder

| | |
|---|---|
| [game.json](game.json) | the discs, their checksums, and the decomp's pinned commit |
| [decomp/](decomp/README.md) | [rac3-decomp](https://github.com/OpenRAC/rac3-decomp), our decomp (git submodule, branch `master`): PAL and NTSC-U |
| `decomp-patches/` | OpenRAC-only changes to `decomp/`, each with its reason (none yet) |

The port's code for PAL is in [port/game/rac3-pal/](../../port/game/rac3-pal/). It reads the
decomp's C as it is, since the decomp names everything by PAL's addresses: no release table is
needed. Of the NTSC-U drafts in `decomp/nonmatching/functional.tsv` it reads only those whose PAL
code is the same as NTSC-U's (`config/us/map.tsv`); `hostgen.json`'s `candidates_left_out` names
the others.

The port's code for NTSC-U is in [port/game/rac3-ntsc/](../../port/game/rac3-ntsc/). It reads
the decomp's C, written with PAL's addresses, in NTSC-U's: `release_names.json` there renames
every name, written by [release_rac3.py](../../port/tools/hostgen/release_rac3.py) from the
decomp's `config/us/map.tsv` and `config/us/names.tsv` (run it again when the pin moves). How to check
the decomp out, change a patch or move its pin: [docs/SOURCES.md](../../docs/SOURCES.md).

## About the decomp

rac3-decomp rebuilds each disc's three core programs byte for byte
([decomp/docs/targets.md](decomp/docs/targets.md)): `frontbin`, the front end and its menus;
`boot_elf`, the main executable (the engine core and a second copy of the front end); and
`i5bootn`, a loader that the disc starts first. It also rebuilds the level programs (49 on PAL,
51 on NTSC-U; [decomp/docs/levels.md](decomp/docs/levels.md)).

- **PAL** is built from C and assembly by `tools/build.py` and `tools/build_levels.py`; every C
  function in `src/` was matched against it.
- **NTSC-U** shares that C wherever its bytes are the same. Its own functions are in `src/us/`,
  its tables in `config/us/`, and `config/us/map.tsv` pairs each PAL function with its NTSC-U
  twin. `tools/asm_build.py --version us --c` rebuilds all 54 NTSC-U programs byte for byte.

It compiles with SN ee-gcc 2.95.3 v1.36 (and Sony's 2.9-ee-991111 for some library code), on
Windows natively and on macOS and Linux through wibo
([decomp/docs/BUILD_FIDELITY.md](decomp/docs/BUILD_FIDELITY.md)). The project is licensed under
the GNU GPL v3 ([decomp/LICENSE](decomp/LICENSE)).

## Getting started

Follow [decomp/README.md](decomp/README.md) and [decomp/docs/wiki/Setup.md](decomp/docs/wiki/Setup.md):
you supply the disc and the compilers ([toolchains/README.md](../../toolchains/README.md)). From
`games/rac3/decomp`:

```sh
python3 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install -r tools/requirements.txt
venv/bin/python tools/setup_asm.py --target all
venv/bin/python tools/build.py --target all -j 8 --toolchain <SN ee-gcc dir> --runner <wibo> --ee29 <2.9-ee dir>
```

It ends with one `MATCH` line per program. NTSC-U's build is in
[decomp/docs/versions.md](decomp/docs/versions.md#building-it).

Disc checksums are in [baserom/README.md](../../baserom/README.md); progress in
[progress/](../../progress/README.md).
